title: How many Container Bookings may one customer hold at the same time?
content:
## Policy clause
Under the Container Bookings product line a customer may hold any number of bookings at the same time; there is no cap on concurrent bookings per customer. Every booking is a separate holding with its own charge account and its own lifecycle. A booking's charge account holds what the booking party owes on that booking: freight, surcharges and fees are booked in, while payments, waivers, premium refunds and roll compensation are booked out. The container ceiling applies to each booking on its own and is set by the booking request admission rules of the tier. Splitting one shipment into several bookings is allowed, and each booking is charged, amended, rolled and cancelled independently.

## The same rule, restated
| Question | Answer under this policy |
|---|---|
| Is there a limit on how many live bookings one customer may hold? | No. No per-customer cap exists. |
| Do two bookings of the same customer share one charge account? | No. Each booking has its own charge account. |
| Does the container ceiling count across all of a customer's bookings? | No. It applies to each booking on its own. |
| May one shipment be spread over several bookings? | Yes. Each resulting booking is then handled on its own. |

## Hypothetical illustration
*Hypothetical figures, for illustration only:* if a tier's per-booking ceiling were 25 containers, a shipper with 40 containers for one sailing could split them into one booking of 25 and one of 15. A later cancellation of the 15-container booking would be charged, and any fee computed, on that booking alone; the 25-container booking would stay live with its own account and lifecycle untouched.
